claim: Cdc48/p97 is a ubiquitin-selective chaperone that orchestrates the function of E3 ligases and deubiquitylases (DUBs).
source: Cdc48/p97, a ubiquitin-selective chaperone, orchestrates the function of E3 ligases and deubiquitylases (DUBs).
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a known function of Cdc48/p97, supported by established scientific knowledge.

claim: Ubp12 and Ubp2 exert opposing effects on mitochondrial fusion.
source: The DUBs Ubp12 and Ubp2 exert opposing effects on mitochondrial fusion and cleave different ubiquitin chains on the mitofusin Fzo1.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented throughout the manuscript showing opposite phenotypes of Ubp12 and Ubp2 deletion on mitochondrial morphology.

claim: Ubp12 and Ubp2 cleave different ubiquitin chains on the mitofusin Fzo1.
source: The DUBs Ubp12 and Ubp2 exert opposing effects on mitochondrial fusion and cleave different ubiquitin chains on the mitofusin Fzo1.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing that Ubp12 and Ubp2 recognize and cleave distinct ubiquitin forms on Fzo1.

claim: Cdc48 integrates the activities of Ubp12 and Ubp2, which are themselves ubiquitylated.
source: We demonstrate that Cdc48 integrates the activities of these two DUBs, which are themselves ubiquitylated.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing physical interactions between Cdc48 and both DUBs, and ubiquitylation of both Ubp12 and Ubp2.

claim: Cdc48 promotes proteolysis of Ubp12.
source: First, Cdc48 promotes proteolysis of Ubp12, stabilizing pro-fusion ubiquitylation on Fzo1.
evidence: This is supported by cycloheximide chase experiments showing that Ubp12 is stabilized in cdc48-2 mutant cells.

claim: Cdc48-mediated proteolysis of Ubp12 stabilizes pro-fusion ubiquitylation on Fzo1.
source: First, Cdc48 promotes proteolysis of Ubp12, stabilizing pro-fusion ubiquitylation on Fzo1.
evidence: This is supported by data showing that deletion of UBP12 in cdc48-2 cells rescues Fzo1 ubiquitylation and mitochondrial tubulation.

claim: Loss of Ubp12 stabilizes Ubp2.
source: Second, loss of Ubp12 stabilizes Ubp2 and thereby facilitates removal of ubiquitin chains on Fzo1 inhibiting fusion.
evidence: This is supported by cycloheximide chase experiments showing that Ubp2 turnover is regulated by Ubp12.

claim: Stabilization of Ubp2 facilitates removal of ubiquitin chains on Fzo1 that inhibit fusion.
source: Second, loss of Ubp12 stabilizes Ubp2 and thereby facilitates removal of ubiquitin chains on Fzo1 inhibiting fusion.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Ubp2 recognizes and cleaves anti-fusion ubiquitin chains on Fzo1, and its stabilization would enhance this activity.

claim: Cdc48 synergistically regulates the ubiquitylation status of Fzo1.
source: Thus, Cdc48 synergistically regulates the ubiquitylation status of Fzo1, allowing to control the balance between activation or repression of mitochondrial fusion.
evidence: This is supported by data showing that Cdc48 affects Fzo1 ubiquitylation through both Ubp12 and Ubp2 pathways.

claim: Cdc48 controls the balance between activation or repression of mitochondrial fusion.
source: Thus, Cdc48 synergistically regulates the ubiquitylation status of Fzo1, allowing to control the balance between activation or repression of mitochondrial fusion.
evidence: This is supported by mitochondrial morphology data showing that Cdc48 mutation leads to fragmented mitochondria, and this phenotype can be rescued by manipulating Ubp12 and Ubp2.

claim: Cdc48, Ubp12, and Ubp2 form a cascade of ubiquitylation events that fine-tunes the fusogenic activity of Fzo1.
source: In conclusion, we unravel a new cascade of ubiquitylation events, comprising Cdc48 and two DUBs, fine-tuning the fusogenic activity of Fzo1.
evidence: This is the main conclusion supported by all experimental data showing the hierarchical regulation between Cdc48, Ubp12, and Ubp2.

claim: Parkin-dependent ubiquitylation of mitochondrial outer membrane proteins modulates the elimination of damaged organelles by mitophagy.
source: For example, Parkin-dependent ubiquitylation of mitochondrial outer membrane (OM) proteins modulates the elimination of the damaged organelles by mitophagy, or via mitochondrial-derived vesicles (MDV) that fuse with the late endosome (Pickrell and Youle, 2015; Sugiura et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Parkin-dependent ubiquitylation of mitochondrial outer membrane proteins modulates the elimination of damaged organelles via mitochondrial-derived vesicles (MDV) that fuse with the late endosome.
source: For example, Parkin-dependent ubiquitylation of mitochondrial outer membrane (OM) proteins modulates the elimination of the damaged organelles by mitophagy, or via mitochondrial-derived vesicles (MDV) that fuse with the late endosome (Pickrell and Youle, 2015; Sugiura et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Most fusion processes, including the Parkin-MDV pathway, rely on SNAREs.
source: Most fusion processes, including the Parkin-MDV pathway, rely on SNAREs (McLelland et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Fusion of the endoplasmic reticulum and of mitochondria depend on large dynamin-related GTPases.
source: In contrast, fusion of the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) and of mitochondria depend on large dynamin-related GTPases (Escobar-Henriques and Anton, 2013; Hu and Rapoport, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: In mitochondria, dynamin-related GTPases are named mitofusins (Mfn1/Mfn2 in mammals, Fzo1 in yeast).
source: In mitochondria, they are named mitofusins (Mfn1/Mfn2 in mammals, Fzo1 in yeast).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about mitochondrial fusion proteins.

claim: Deficiencies in Mfn2 cause the type 2 subset of the Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (CMT).
source: Deficiencies in Mfn2 cause the type 2 subset of the Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (CMT), the most common degenerative disorder of the peripheral nervous system (Züchner et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (CMT) is the most common degenerative disorder of the peripheral nervous system.
source: Deficiencies in Mfn2 cause the type 2 subset of the Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (CMT), the most common degenerative disorder of the peripheral nervous system (Züchner et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The ubiquitin-specific chaperone Cdc48/p97 is required to maintain mitochondrial morphology.
source: The ubiquitin-specific chaperone Cdc48/p97 is required to maintain mitochondrial morphology (Esaki and Ogura, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The molecular mechanism of how Cdc48 regulates mitochondrial dynamics is not understood.
source: However, the underlying molecular mechanism of how Cdc48 regulates mitochondrial dynamics is not understood.
evidence: This statement identifies a gap in knowledge that the current study addresses.

claim: Cdc48 is an essential AAA-ATPase.
source: Cdc48 is an essential AAA-ATPase and one of the most abundant proteins in the cell, which recognizes many ubiquitylated substrates and is involved in a myriad of biological processes (Franz et al., 2014; Meyer and Weihl, 2014).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Cdc48 is one of the most abundant proteins in the cell.
source: Cdc48 is an essential AAA-ATPase and one of the most abundant proteins in the cell, which recognizes many ubiquitylated substrates and is involved in a myriad of biological processes (Franz et al., 2014; Meyer and Weihl, 2014).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Cdc48 recognizes many ubiquitylated substrates.
source: Cdc48 is an essential AAA-ATPase and one of the most abundant proteins in the cell, which recognizes many ubiquitylated substrates and is involved in a myriad of biological processes (Franz et al., 2014; Meyer and Weihl, 2014).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Cdc48 is involved in a myriad of biological processes.
source: Cdc48 is an essential AAA-ATPase and one of the most abundant proteins in the cell, which recognizes many ubiquitylated substrates and is involved in a myriad of biological processes (Franz et al., 2014; Meyer and Weihl, 2014).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Cdc48 segregates ubiquitylated substrates from protein complexes or from membranes, thus allowing their proteolysis by the proteasome.
source: Cdc48 segregates ubiquitylated substrates from protein complexes, or from membranes, thus allowing their proteolysis by the proteasome (Franz et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Cdc48 is important for ER-associated protein degradation (ERAD).
source: For example, Cdc48 is important for ER-associated protein degradation (ERAD), modulates the turnover of mitochondrial OM proteins (OMMAD), participates in apoptosis responses (Laun et al., 2001) and mediates clearance of damaged lysosomes by autophagy (Avci and Lemberg, 2015; Heo et al., 2010; Papadopoulos et al., 2017; Tanaka et al., 2010; Wu et al., 2016; Xu et al., 2011; Zattas and Hochstrasser, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Cdc48 modulates the turnover of mitochondrial OM proteins (OMMAD).
source: For example, Cdc48 is important for ER-associated protein degradation (ERAD), modulates the turnover of mitochondrial OM proteins (OMMAD), participates in apoptosis responses (Laun et al., 2001) and mediates clearance of damaged lysosomes by autophagy (Avci and Lemberg, 2015; Heo et al., 2010; Papadopoulos et al., 2017; Tanaka et al., 2010; Wu et al., 2016; Xu et al., 2011; Zattas and Hochstrasser, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Cdc48 participates in apoptosis responses.
source: For example, Cdc48 is important for ER-associated protein degradation (ERAD), modulates the turnover of mitochondrial OM proteins (OMMAD), participates in apoptosis responses (Laun et al., 2001) and mediates clearance of damaged lysosomes by autophagy (Avci and Lemberg, 2015; Heo et al., 2010; Papadopoulos et al., 2017; Tanaka et al., 2010; Wu et al., 2016; Xu et al., 2011; Zattas and Hochstrasser, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Cdc48 mediates clearance of damaged lysosomes by autophagy.
source: For example, Cdc48 is important for ER-associated protein degradation (ERAD), modulates the turnover of mitochondrial OM proteins (OMMAD), participates in apoptosis responses (Laun et al., 2001) and mediates clearance of damaged lysosomes by autophagy (Avci and Lemberg, 2015; Heo et al., 2010; Papadopoulos et al., 2017; Tanaka et al., 2010; Wu et al., 2016; Xu et al., 2011; Zattas and Hochstrasser, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Cdc48 binds E3 ubiquitin ligases and deubiquitylases (DUBs) thereby regulating substrate ubiquitylation.
source: On the other hand, Cdc48 also binds E3 ubiquitin ligases and deubiquitylases (DUBs) thereby regulating substrate ubiquitylation (Meyer and Weihl, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: DUBs are proteases that catalyze the reversion of the ubiquitylation reaction.
source: DUBs are proteases that catalyze the reversion of the ubiquitylation reaction (Love et al., 2007), critically contributing to ubiquitin homeostasis (Amerik and Hochstrasser, 2004; Kimura and Tanaka, 2010; Park and Ryu, 2014; Swatek and Komander, 2016).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: DUBs critically contribute to ubiquitin homeostasis.
source: DUBs are proteases that catalyze the reversion of the ubiquitylation reaction (Love et al., 2007), critically contributing to ubiquitin homeostasis (Amerik and Hochstrasser, 2004; Kimura and Tanaka, 2010; Park and Ryu, 2014; Swatek and Komander, 2016).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: DUBs activate ubiquitin by releasing it from ubiquitin precursor polypeptides.
source: DUBs activate ubiquitin by releasing it from ubiquitin precursor polypeptides but are also determinants for the modification status of ubiquitylated substrates, allowing to dampen ubiquitin-mediated events (Clague et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: DUBs are determinants for the modification status of ubiquitylated substrates, allowing to dampen ubiquitin-mediated events.
source: DUBs activate ubiquitin by releasing it from ubiquitin precursor polypeptides but are also determinants for the modification status of ubiquitylated substrates, allowing to dampen ubiquitin-mediated events (Clague et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: DUBs are associated with a number of human diseases.
source: Importantly, DUBs are associated with a number of human diseases and represent promising drug targets, whose regulation and mechanism of action need to be explored (Heideker and Wertz, 2015; Sahtoe and Sixma, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: DUBs represent promising drug targets.
source: Importantly, DUBs are associated with a number of human diseases and represent promising drug targets, whose regulation and mechanism of action need to be explored (Heideker and Wertz, 2015; Sahtoe and Sixma, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Two deubiquitylases, Ubp2 and Ubp12, were found to have opposite effects on mitochondrial morphology.
source: Two deubiquitylases, Ubp2 and Ubp12, were found to have opposite effects on mitochondrial morphology (Anton et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Ubiquitin chains on Fzo1 that are recognized and cleaved by Ubp12 activate mitochondrial fusion.
source: Ubiquitin chains on Fzo1 that are recognized and cleaved by Ubp12 activate mitochondrial fusion.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature (Anton et al., 2013).

claim: Ubiquitin chains on Fzo1 that are recognized and cleaved by Ubp2 target Fzo1 for proteasomal degradation and inhibit mitochondrial fusion.
source: In contrast, other ubiquitin chains on Fzo1 that instead are recognized and cleaved by Ubp2 target Fzo1 for proteasomal degradation and inhibit mitochondrial fusion.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature (Anton et al., 2013).

claim: Ubiquitin is a double-faced regulator of mitochondrial fusion.
source: Therefore, although it is clear that ubiquitin is a double-faced regulator of mitochondrial fusion (Escobar-Henriques and Langer, 2014), how Ubp2 and Ubp12 exert opposite effects on Fzo1 and mitochondrial fusion remained poorly studied.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Cdc48 negatively regulates Ubp12.
source: Cdc48 negatively regulates Ubp12, which negatively regulates Ubp2, explaining why these two DUBs exert opposite effects on their targets and on ubiquitin homeostasis.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing that Cdc48 promotes degradation of Ubp12.

claim: Ubp12 negatively regulates Ubp2.
source: Cdc48 negatively regulates Ubp12, which negatively regulates Ubp2, explaining why these two DUBs exert opposite effects on their targets and on ubiquitin homeostasis.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing that Ubp12 promotes degradation of Ubp2.

claim: cdc48-2 cells present fragmented mitochondria.
source: We observed that cdc48-2 cells presented fragmented mitochondria (Figure 1A), consistent with the mitochondrial phenotypes observed upon impairment of the ATPase activity of Cdc48 (Esaki and Ogura, 2012).
evidence: This is directly observed in microscopy data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Fragmented mitochondria in cdc48-2 cells is consistent with mitochondrial phenotypes observed upon impairment of the ATPase activity of Cdc48.
source: We observed that cdc48-2 cells presented fragmented mitochondria (Figure 1A), consistent with the mitochondrial phenotypes observed upon impairment of the ATPase activity of Cdc48 (Esaki and Ogura, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Fzo1 ubiquitylation is decreased in cdc48-2 mutant cells compared to wild-type cells.
source: Consistent with mitochondrial fragmentation, we observed a decrease of Fzo1 ubiquitylation in cdc48-2 mutant cells, when compared to wild-type (wt) cells (Figure 1B, black arrows).
evidence: This is directly observed in the immunoblot data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Pro-fusion ubiquitylation of Fzo1 increases its stability.
source: We have previously shown that pro-fusion ubiquitylation of Fzo1 increases its stability (Anton et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The steady state levels of Fzo1 and its ubiquitylated forms are decreased in cdc48-2 cells.
source: Accordingly, the steady state levels of Fzo1 and its ubiquitylated forms were decreased in cdc48-2 cells (compare Figure 1C and B), to a similar and not significantly different extent (data not shown).
evidence: This is directly observed in the immunoblot data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The levels of Fzo1 are slightly decreased in the cdc48-3 mutant.
source: Consistent with the cdc48-2 allele, the levels of Fzo1 were slightly decreased in the cdc48-3 mutant or in cells deleted for the Cdc48 co-factors Npl4, Ufd1 and Ufd3/Doa1 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: This is directly observed in the immunoblot data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–C.

claim: The levels of Fzo1 are slightly decreased in cells deleted for the Cdc48 co-factors Npl4, Ufd1 and Ufd3/Doa1.
source: Consistent with the cdc48-2 allele, the levels of Fzo1 were slightly decreased in the cdc48-3 mutant or in cells deleted for the Cdc48 co-factors Npl4, Ufd1 and Ufd3/Doa1 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: This is directly observed in the immunoblot data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–C.

claim: Ubc6 is degraded by the proteasome via ERAD, a process dependent on Cdc48.
source: It was previously shown that Ubc6, an endoplasmic reticulum (ER) membrane protein, is degraded by the proteasome via ERAD, a process dependent on Cdc48 (Lenk et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The steady state levels of Ubc6 are increased upon impairment of Cdc48 activity.
source: As expected, and in contrast to Fzo1, the steady state levels of Ubc6 were increased upon impairment of Cdc48 activity (Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: This is directly observed in the immunoblot data shown in Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–C.

claim: Cdc48 regulates Fzo1 by a mechanism different from OMMAD or ERAD.
source: This suggested that Cdc48 regulates Fzo1 by a mechanism different from OMMAD or ERAD.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Fzo1 and Ubc6 respond oppositely to Cdc48 impairment.

claim: Fzo1 degradation is inhibited by the proteasome inhibitor MG132 in cdc48-2 cells.
source: We observed that Fzo1 degradation was inhibited by the presence of the proteasome inhibitor MG132, indicating that the decreased levels of Fzo1 observed in cdc48-2 cells were due to proteasome-dependent turnover of Fzo1 (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is directly observed in the cycloheximide chase experiment shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The decreased levels of Fzo1 observed in cdc48-2 cells are due to proteasome-dependent turnover of Fzo1.
source: We observed that Fzo1 degradation was inhibited by the presence of the proteasome inhibitor MG132, indicating that the decreased levels of Fzo1 observed in cdc48-2 cells were due to proteasome-dependent turnover of Fzo1 (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that MG132 inhibits Fzo1 degradation in cdc48-2 cells.

claim: Proteasome inhibition does not affect Fzo1 turnover in wild-type cells.
source: In contrast, proteasome inhibition did not affect Fzo1 turnover in wt cells consistent with previous observations (Anton et al., 2013; Escobar-Henriques et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1D and citations to previous literature.

claim: Expression of wild-type Cdc48 protein rescues the phenotypes of cdc48-2 cells.
source: Importantly, all these phenotypes could be rescued by expression of the wt Cdc48 protein but not by expression of the Cdc48A547T variant, mimicking the specific mutation in cdc48-2 (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A–C).
evidence: This is directly observed in the rescue experiments shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A–C.

claim: Expression of the Cdc48A547T variant does not rescue the phenotypes of cdc48-2 cells.
source: Importantly, all these phenotypes could be rescued by expression of the wt Cdc48 protein but not by expression of the Cdc48A547T variant, mimicking the specific mutation in cdc48-2 (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A–C).
evidence: This is directly observed in the rescue experiments shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A–C.

claim: Cdc48 is required to maintain the Fzo1 protein, thus promoting mitochondrial fusion events.
source: In conclusion, Cdc48 is required to maintain the Fzo1 protein, thus promoting mitochondrial fusion events.
evidence: This is the conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing that Cdc48 mutation leads to decreased Fzo1 levels and fragmented mitochondria.

claim: Cdc48 physically interacts with Fzo1.
source: First, co-immunoprecipitation experiments revealed that Cdc48 physically interacted with Fzo1 (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is directly observed in the co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The formation of ubiquitin chains on Fzo1 linked to lysine 398 requires previous ubiquitylation of its lysine 464.
source: We previously showed that the formation of ubiquitin chains on Fzo1 (Figure 2A, black arrows), which are linked to lysine 398, requires previous ubiquitylation of its lysine 464 (Anton et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Fzo1 ubiquitylation is lost in the mutant Fzo1K464R.
source: Therefore, Fzo1 ubiquitylation is lost in the mutant Fzo1K464R (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is directly observed in the immunoblot data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The interaction between Cdc48 and the non-ubiquitylated variant Fzo1K464R is impaired.
source: We observed that the interaction between Cdc48 and the non-ubiquitylated variant Fzo1K464R was impaired (Figure 2A), in agreement with ubiquitin being recognized by Cdc48.
evidence: This is directly observed in the co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The steady state levels of Fzo1K464R are largely insensitive to the cdc48-2 mutation.
source: We observed that the steady state levels of Fzo1K464R were largely insensitive to the cdc48-2 mutation (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is directly observed in the immunoblot data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Cdc48 has a direct regulatory role on Fzo1, only after its ubiquitylation.
source: This points to a direct regulatory role of Cdc48 on Fzo1, only after its ubiquitylation.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Fzo1K464R is insensitive to cdc48-2 mutation.

claim: Expression of Ubp2C745S leads to accumulation of ubiquitylated forms of Fzo1 that inhibit fusion.
source: In addition, we previously identified other ubiquitin forms on Fzo1, that inhibit fusion. They are removed by Ubp2 and can be detected only in the presence of the catalytically inactive variant Ubp2C745S (Anton et al., 2013) (Figure 2B, Input, red arrows).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature and data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Despite the increase in ubiquitylation of Fzo1 upon Ubp2C745S expression, Cdc48 binding to Fzo1 is not increased.
source: We noticed that despite the clear increase in ubiquitylation of Fzo1 upon Ubp2C745S expression (2.44 times), Cdc48 binding to Fzo1 was not increased (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is directly observed in the co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The additional presence of ubiquitin chains inhibiting fusion does not increase Cdc48 binding to Fzo1.
source: Therefore, the additional presence of ubiquitin chains inhibiting fusion does not increase Cdc48 binding.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Ubp2C745S expression increases Fzo1 ubiquitylation but not Cdc48 binding.

claim: For the Fzo1K464R variant, which in the presence of Ubp2C745S is ubiquitylated to a similar level as the wild-type protein, no binding to Cdc48 above background can be detected.
source: Consistently, for the Fzo1K464R variant, which in the presence of Ubp2C745S is ubiquitylated to a similar level as the wt protein (0.96 times, despite the absence of pro-fusion ubiquitylation), no binding to Cdc48 above background can be detected.
evidence: This is directly observed in the co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Similar to Ubp12, Cdc48 recognizes specifically the pro-fusion ubiquitylated forms of Fzo1.
source: Thus, similar to Ubp12, Cdc48 recognizes specifically the pro-fusion ubiquitylated forms of Fzo1.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Cdc48 binding to Fzo1 depends on K464-dependent ubiquitylation.

claim: Ubp12 is degraded in a Cdc48-dependent manner.
source: CHX chase experiments revealed that Ubp12 is degraded in a Cdc48- and proteasome-dependent manner (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This is directly observed in the cycloheximide chase experiments shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: Ubp12 is degraded in a proteasome-dependent manner.
source: CHX chase experiments revealed that Ubp12 is degraded in a Cdc48- and proteasome-dependent manner (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This is directly observed in the cycloheximide chase experiments shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: Chromosomally tagged Ubp12 is an unstable protein.
source: Similarly, chromosomally tagged Ubp12 is an unstable protein and its turnover depends on Cdc48 (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is directly observed in the cycloheximide chase experiment shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The turnover of chromosomally tagged Ubp12 depends on Cdc48.
source: Similarly, chromosomally tagged Ubp12 is an unstable protein and its turnover depends on Cdc48 (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is directly observed in the cycloheximide chase experiment shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Ubp12 is modified by ubiquitin.
source: We observed slower migrating forms of Ubp12 with the Flag-specific antibody, which were also detected by a ubiquitin-specific antibody. These studies demonstrated that Ubp12 is modified by ubiquitin.
evidence: This is directly observed in the immunoprecipitation and immunoblot data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Ubp12 physically interacts with Cdc48.
source: We observed that Ubp12 physically interacted with Cdc48 (Figure 3C), suggesting that Cdc48 directly supports degradation of ubiquitylated Ubp12.
evidence: This is directly observed in the co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Cdc48 directly supports degradation of ubiquitylated Ubp12.
source: We observed that Ubp12 physically interacted with Cdc48 (Figure 3C), suggesting that Cdc48 directly supports degradation of ubiquitylated Ubp12.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Ubp12 is ubiquitylated, interacts with Cdc48, and its degradation depends on Cdc48.

claim: Cdc48 and Ubp12 have opposing roles on Fzo1 ubiquitylation levels.
source: Our results show that Cdc48 and Ubp12 have opposing roles on Fzo1 ubiquitylation levels (Figure 1B and [Anton et al., 2013]).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1B and a citation to previous literature.

claim: Ubp12 and Cdc48 present opposing phenotypes regarding mitochondrial tubulation.
source: Consistently, Ubp12 and Cdc48 also present opposing phenotypes regarding mitochondrial tubulation (Figure 1A and [Anton et al., 2013]).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1A and a citation to previous literature.

claim: Deletion of UBP12 in cdc48-2 cells rescues mitochondrial tubulation.
source: Strikingly, deletion of UBP12 in cdc48-2 cells rescued mitochondrial tubulation, resembling Δubp12 cells (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is directly observed in the microscopy data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The mitochondrial hypertubulation of Δubp12 cells depends on Fzo1.
source: Importantly, the mitochondrial hypertubulation of Δubp12 cells depended on Fzo1 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: This is directly observed in the microscopy data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–C.

claim: In Δfzo1 Δdnm1 cells, further deletion of UBP12 does not induce hypertubulation.
source: Even in Δfzo1 Δdnm1 cells, resembling wt cells in mitochondrial shape, further deletion of UBP12 did not induce hypertubulation, confirming that Ubp12 regulates mitochondrial morphology via Fzo1 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is directly observed in the microscopy data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Ubp12 regulates mitochondrial morphology via Fzo1.
source: Even in Δfzo1 Δdnm1 cells, resembling wt cells in mitochondrial shape, further deletion of UBP12 did not induce hypertubulation, confirming that Ubp12 regulates mitochondrial morphology via Fzo1 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Ubp12 deletion does not affect mitochondrial morphology in the absence of Fzo1.

claim: Mitochondrial fusion is required to maintain cellular growth on respiratory media containing non-fermentable carbon sources glycerol or lactate.
source: Mitochondrial fusion is also required to maintain the cellular growth on respiratory media, i.e. media containing the non-fermentable carbon sources glycerol or lactate (Hermann et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The growth defect of cdc48-2 cells at 37°C on lactate media can be improved upon deletion of UBP12.
source: In agreement with restored tubulation of mitochondria, we observed that the growth defect of cdc48-2 cells at 37°C on lactate media could be improved upon deletion of UBP12 (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is directly observed in the spot assay shown in Figure 4B.

claim: cdc48-2 cells do not lose mitochondrial DNA.
source: Consistent with the respiratory reversibility of cdc48-2 cells upon further deletion of UBP12, we observed that cdc48-2 cells did not lose mitochondrial DNA (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A and B).
evidence: This is directly observed in the RT-PCR and immunoblot data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A and B.

claim: The respiratory defect of cdc48-2 cells can be complemented by expression of Cdc48 but not of Cdc48A547T.
source: Importantly, the respiratory defect of cdc48-2 cells could be complemented by expression of Cdc48 but not of Cdc48A547T (Figure 4—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is directly observed in the spot assay shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2C.

claim: cdc48-2Δubp12 cells show improved ubiquitylation of Fzo1.
source: Finally, cdc48-2Δubp12 cells also showed improved ubiquitylation of Fzo1 (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is directly observed in the immunoblot data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Cdc48 maintains Fzo1 ubiquitylation and activates mitochondrial fusion by downregulating Ubp12.
source: Together, these results show that Cdc48 maintains Fzo1 ubiquitylation and activates mitochondrial fusion by downregulating Ubp12.
evidence: This is the conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing that deletion of UBP12 rescues cdc48-2 phenotypes.

claim: The physical interaction between Fzo1 and Cdc48 is not mediated by Ubp12.
source: First, we observed that the physical interaction between Fzo1 and Cdc48 is not mediated by Ubp12 (Figure 4—figure supplement 2D), suggesting that Cdc48 directly recognizes ubiquitylated Fzo1.
evidence: This is directly observed in the co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2D.

claim: Cdc48 directly recognizes ubiquitylated Fzo1.
source: First, we observed that the physical interaction between Fzo1 and Cdc48 is not mediated by Ubp12 (Figure 4—figure supplement 2D), suggesting that Cdc48 directly recognizes ubiquitylated Fzo1.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Cdc48-Fzo1 interaction is not mediated by Ubp12.

claim: Deletion of UBP12 in cdc48-2 cells does not restore the steady state levels of Fzo1.
source: Second, deletion of UBP12 in cdc48-2 cells did not restore the steady state levels of Fzo1 (Figure 4—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This is directly observed in the immunoblot data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2E.

claim: Mitochondrial fusion depends on ubiquitylated rather than on the steady state levels of Fzo1.
source: Notably, this is consistent with our previous observation that mitochondrial fusion depends on ubiquitylated rather than on the steady state levels of Fzo1 (Anton et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Increased levels of Fzo1 present in ∆ubp12 cells specifically depend on Ubp2.
source: We noticed that increased levels of Fzo1, present in ∆ubp12 cells, specifically depended on Ubp2 (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is directly observed in the immunoblot data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Ubp12 and Ubp2 are interdependent.
source: Therefore, Ubp12 and Ubp2, which affect the stability of Fzo1 in opposite manners, are also interdependent.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Fzo1 levels in Δubp12 cells depend on Ubp2.

claim: Ubp2 and Ubp12 have opposite phenotypes related to ubiquitin homeostasis.
source: We observed that indeed Ubp2 and Ubp12 had opposite phenotypes (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is directly observed in the CHX resistance assay and ubiquitin level analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Ubp2 is an unstable protein.
source: We tested if Ubp2 is an unstable protein and whether Ubp12 is involved in its degradation, after inhibition of protein synthesis with CHX. The levels of genomically tagged Ubp2 decreased over time and Ubp2-turnover was regulated by Ubp12 (Figure 5B) and by the proteasome (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is directly observed in the cycloheximide chase experiment shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Ubp2 turnover is regulated by Ubp12.
source: We tested if Ubp2 is an unstable protein and whether Ubp12 is involved in its degradation, after inhibition of protein synthesis with CHX. The levels of genomically tagged Ubp2 decreased over time and Ubp2-turnover was regulated by Ubp12 (Figure 5B) and by the proteasome (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is directly observed in the cycloheximide chase experiment shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Ubp2 turnover is regulated by the proteasome.
source: We tested if Ubp2 is an unstable protein and whether Ubp12 is involved in its degradation, after inhibition of protein synthesis with CHX. The levels of genomically tagged Ubp2 decreased over time and Ubp2-turnover was regulated by Ubp12 (Figure 5B) and by the proteasome (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is directly observed in the cycloheximide chase experiment shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Ubp2 interacts with Ubp12.
source: Moreover, co-immunoprecipitation experiments revealed that Ubp2 interacted with Ubp12, suggesting a direct regulation between both DUBs (Figure 5—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is directly observed in the co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2B.

claim: There is a direct regulation between Ubp2 and Ubp12.
source: Moreover, co-immunoprecipitation experiments revealed that Ubp2 interacted with Ubp12, suggesting a direct regulation between both DUBs (Figure 5—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Ubp2 and Ubp12 physically interact.

claim: Ubp2 is ubiquitylated.
source: After immunoprecipitation of Ubp2-Flag, and consistent with recent observations (Cavellini et al., 2017), we observed the presence of slowly migrating forms of Ubp2 during electrophoresis, in wt cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 2C) but mostly in Δubp12 cells (Figure 5C, left panel). Importantly, we show that these forms could also be detected using a ubiquitin-specific antibody, demonstrating that they represent ubiquitylated Ubp2 (Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 2C, right panels).
evidence: This is directly observed in the immunoprecipitation and immunoblot data shown in Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 2C.

claim: Ubp12 mediates deubiquitylation of Ubp2.
source: This indicates that Ubp12 mediates deubiquitylation of Ubp2 and suggests that Ubp2 acts downstream of Ubp12, thus revealing a hierarchical cascade between DUBs, of relevance for the protein levels of Fzo1 and for ubiquitin homeostasis.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Ubp2 ubiquitylation accumulates in Δubp12 cells.

claim: Ubp2 acts downstream of Ubp12.
source: This indicates that Ubp12 mediates deubiquitylation of Ubp2 and suggests that Ubp2 acts downstream of Ubp12, thus revealing a hierarchical cascade between DUBs, of relevance for the protein levels of Fzo1 and for ubiquitin homeostasis.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Ubp12 regulates Ubp2 ubiquitylation and stability.

claim: There is a hierarchical cascade between Ubp12 and Ubp2.
source: This indicates that Ubp12 mediates deubiquitylation of Ubp2 and suggests that Ubp2 acts downstream of Ubp12, thus revealing a hierarchical cascade between DUBs, of relevance for the protein levels of Fzo1 and for ubiquitin homeostasis.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Ubp12 regulates Ubp2.

claim: Overexpression of ubiquitin mutated in K48R strongly decreases Fzo1 ubiquitylation.
source: Overexpression of ubiquitin mutated in K48R strongly decreased Fzo1 and Ubp2 ubiquitylation, revealing that their ubiquitin chains are linked via K48 (Figure 6A and C).
evidence: This is directly observed in the immunoblot data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Overexpression of ubiquitin mutated in K48R strongly decreases Ubp2 ubiquitylation.
source: Overexpression of ubiquitin mutated in K48R strongly decreased Fzo1 and Ubp2 ubiquitylation, revealing that their ubiquitin chains are linked via K48 (Figure 6A and C).
evidence: This is directly observed in the immunoblot data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The ubiquitin chains on Fzo1 recognized by Ubp12 are linked via K48.
source: Overexpression of ubiquitin mutated in K48R strongly decreased Fzo1 and Ubp2 ubiquitylation, revealing that their ubiquitin chains are linked via K48 (Figure 6A and C).
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that K48R ubiquitin mutation decreases Fzo1 ubiquitylation in Δubp12 cells.

claim: The ubiquitin chains on Ubp2 are linked via K48.
source: Overexpression of ubiquitin mutated in K48R strongly decreased Fzo1 and Ubp2 ubiquitylation, revealing that their ubiquitin chains are linked via K48 (Figure 6A and C).
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that K48R ubiquitin mutation decreases Ubp2 ubiquitylation.

claim: The ubiquitin chains on Fzo1 that destabilize it and inhibit fusion are K48-linked.
source: However, the ubiquitin chains on Fzo1 that destabilize it and inhibit fusion, which are not bound by Ubp12, are also K48-linked (Figure 6B) (Anton et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6B and a citation to previous literature.

claim: Ubp12 reveals no chain preference in vitro when using K48-linked or K63-linked ubiquitin chains.
source: However, in all cases, Ubp12 revealed no chain preference (Figure 6D,E).
evidence: This is directly observed in the in vitro deubiquitylation assays shown in Figure 6D and E.

claim: The K48 chains on Fzo1 consist of two ubiquitin moieties.
source: These results suggest that the K48 chains on Fzo1 consist of two ubiquitin moieties.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that co-expression of tagged and non-tagged ubiquitin reveals only two additional bands above each ubiquitylated form of Fzo1.

claim: Ubp12 recognizes ubiquitylated chains on Fzo1 composed of a very small number of ubiquitin moieties.
source: In conclusion, Ubp12 recognizes ubiquitylated chains on Fzo1 composed of a very small number of ubiquitin moieties.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Fzo1 ubiquitin chains consist of two ubiquitin moieties.

claim: Ubp12 does not stabilize its substrates because their ubiquitin chains are too short to target proteasomal turnover.
source: We therefore propose that Ubp12 does not stabilize its substrates because their ubiquitin chains are too short to target proteasomal turnover.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on the observation that Ubp12 recognizes short ubiquitin chains.

claim: Ubp2-specific ubiquitylation of Fzo1 largely depends on Ubp12-specific ubiquitylation of Fzo1.
source: We conclude that Ubp2-specific ubiquitylation of Fzo1 largely depends on Ubp12-specific ubiquitylation of Fzo1, indicating a regulatory cascade of Ubp12 and Ubp2 on Fzo1.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that anti-fusion ubiquitylation of Fzo1 is reduced in the Fzo1K464R mutant.

claim: Pro-fusion ubiquitylation of Fzo1 primes Fzo1 for the formation of anti-fusion ubiquitylation.
source: This shows that Ubp2-dependent ubiquitylation largely requires previous K464-dependent ubiquitylation . Therefore, pro-fusion ubiquitylation, which stabilizes Fzo1, primes Fzo1 for the formation of anti-fusion ubiquitylation.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that anti-fusion ubiquitylation depends on K464-dependent ubiquitylation.

claim: In ∆ubp2 ∆ubp12 cells, the steady state levels of Fzo1 are insensitive to further mutating Cdc48.
source: Indeed, and in contrast to wt cells, in ∆ubp2 ∆ubp12 cells the steady state levels of Fzo1 were insensitive to further mutating Cdc48 (Figure 8A).
evidence: This is directly observed in the immunoblot data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: ∆ubp2 cells are insensitive to the presence of the cdc48-2 allele.
source: Moreover, ∆ubp2 cells and ∆ubp2 ∆ubp12 were similarly insensitive to the presence of the cdc48-2 allele (Figure 8B), consistent with the UBP2 UBP12 epistasis results (Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This is directly observed in the immunoblot data shown in Figure 8B.

claim: Overexpression of Ubp2 improves mitochondrial tubulation in cdc48-2 cells.
source: Consistently, mitochondrial tubulation was significantly improved under these conditions (Figure 8C).
evidence: This is directly observed in the microscopy data shown in Figure 8C.

claim: Ubp2 overexpression improves the growth defect of cdc48-2 cells on lactate media at 37°C.
source: Moreover, Ubp2 overexpression improved the growth defect of cdc48-2 cells on lactate media at the non-permissive temperature of 37°C, supporting the physiological impact of the Ubp2 levels in cdc48-2 cells (Figure 8D).
evidence: This is directly observed in the spot assay shown in Figure 8D.

claim: A physical interaction between Ubp2 and Cdc48 can be observed.
source: Finally, a physical interaction between Ubp2 and Cdc48 could be observed (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is directly observed in the co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: Cdc48, Ubp12 and Ubp2 orchestrate a multilayered cascade regulation, culminating on Fzo1 ubiquitylation and mitochondrial fusion.
source: Together our results highlight a model in which Cdc48, Ubp12 and Ubp2 orchestrate a multilayered cascade regulation, culminating on Fzo1 ubiquitylation and mitochondrial fusion.
evidence: This is the main conclusion drawn from all experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Cdc48 promotes degradation of Ubp12, controlling Fzo1 ubiquitylation.
source: Cdc48 promotes degradation of Ubp12, controlling Fzo1 ubiquitylation.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing Cdc48-dependent degradation of Ubp12.

claim: Ubp12 prevents mitochondrial fusion by removing the ubiquitylation on Fzo1 that is required for fusion.
source: Ubp12 prevents mitochondrial fusion by two means. On the one hand, it removes the ubiquitylation on Fzo1 that is required for fusion.
evidence: This is supported by data showing that Ubp12 cleaves pro-fusion ubiquitin chains on Fzo1.

claim: Ubp12 promotes degradation of Ubp2.
source: On the other hand, it promotes degradation of Ubp2.
evidence: This is supported by data showing that Ubp2 is stabilized in Δubp12 cells.

claim: By supporting turnover of Ubp12, Cdc48 dually preserves mitochondrial fusion events.
source: Therefore, by supporting turnover of Ubp12, Cdc48 dually preserves mitochondrial fusion events.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Cdc48 regulates both Ubp12 and, indirectly, Ubp2.

claim: The Cdc48-Ubp12-Ubp2 cascade allows fine-tuning of substrate ubiquitylation and modulation of biological processes.
source: Moreover, the Cdc48-Ubp12-Ubp2 cascade allows fine-tuning of substrate ubiquitylation and modulation of the biological processes thereof, as exemplified for Fzo1 and mitochondrial fusion (Figure 9).
evidence: This is the conclusion drawn from all experimental data and illustrated in Figure 9.

claim: Cdc48/p97 extracts ubiquitylated substrates from membranes, thus allowing their recognition and degradation by the proteasome.
source: Cdc48/p97 extracts ubiquitylated substrates from membranes, thus allowing their recognition and degradation by the proteasome (Franz et al., 2014; Rape et al., 2001).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Cdc48/p97 and ubiquitin regulate mitochondrial fusion in both yeast and mammals.
source: Therefore, Cdc48/p97 and ubiquitin regulate mitochondrial fusion in both yeast and mammals.
evidence: This is inferred from the data presented and previous literature.

claim: Eukaryotes present a similar ubiquitin pattern of mitofusins.
source: Moreover, eukaryotes present a similar ubiquitin pattern of mitofusins, suggesting that the new function of Cdc48 presented here could be conserved in mammals under non-damaging conditions.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on the similarity of ubiquitin patterns.

claim: The new function of Cdc48 presented here could be conserved in mammals under non-damaging conditions.
source: Moreover, eukaryotes present a similar ubiquitin pattern of mitofusins, suggesting that the new function of Cdc48 presented here could be conserved in mammals under non-damaging conditions.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on the similarity of ubiquitin patterns.

claim: Mitochondrial fusion is a complex multistep process dependent on sequential events involving GTP binding and hydrolysis by Fzo1, Fzo1 oligomerization and ubiquitylation of Fzo1.
source: Mitochondrial fusion is a complex multistep process dependent on sequential events involving GTP binding and hydrolysis by Fzo1, Fzo1 oligomerization and finally ubiquitylation of Fzo1 (Anton et al., 2011; Brandt et al., 2016; Cohen et al., 2011; Ishihara et al., 2004).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Ubiquitin critically determines mitochondrial fusion events.
source: Although it is clear that ubiquitin critically determines mitochondrial fusion events, the underlying mechanisms are largely unknown (Anton et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: On Fzo1, Ubp12-specific ubiquitylation precedes Ubp2-specific ubiquitylation.
source: Here, given that Ubp12 regulates Ubp2, we show that these two ubiquitylation pathways are connected. Consistently, on Fzo1, Ubp12-specific ubiquitylation also precedes Ubp2-specific ubiquitylation.
evidence: This is supported by data showing that anti-fusion ubiquitylation depends on pro-fusion ubiquitylation.

claim: Unopposed anti-fusion ubiquitylation disrupts mitochondrial tubulation.
source: In fact, unopposed anti-fusion ubiquitylation, as it is the case in Δubp2 cells, disrupts mitochondrial tubulation.
evidence: This is supported by data showing that Δubp2 cells have fragmented mitochondria.

claim: The Ubp12-Ubp2 cascade ensures a tight control of Fzo1 ubiquitylation at levels sufficient to allow mitochondrial fusion but preventing unnecessary ubiquitylation that targets Fzo1 for proteasomal turnover.
source: We conclude that this cascade ensures a tight control of Fzo1 ubiquitylation at levels sufficient to allow mitochondrial fusion but preventing unnecessary ubiquitylation that instead targets Fzo1 for proteasomal turnover.
evidence: This is the conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing the regulatory cascade.

claim: Mdm30 catalyzes the formation of the pro-fusion ubiquitin forms on Fzo1.
source: Mdm30 catalyzes the formation of the pro-fusion ubiquitin forms on Fzo1 (Cohen et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The pro-fusion ubiquitin forms on Fzo1 are bound and cleaved by Ubp12.
source: The pro-fusion forms are bound and cleaved by Ubp12, depend on lysine 464 of Fzo1, and are essential for mitochondrial fusion (Anton et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The pro-fusion ubiquitin forms on Fzo1 depend on lysine 464 of Fzo1.
source: The pro-fusion forms are bound and cleaved by Ubp12, depend on lysine 464 of Fzo1, and are essential for mitochondrial fusion (Anton et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The pro-fusion ubiquitin forms on Fzo1 are essential for mitochondrial fusion.
source: The pro-fusion forms are bound and cleaved by Ubp12, depend on lysine 464 of Fzo1, and are essential for mitochondrial fusion (Anton et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The anti-fusion ubiquitin forms on Fzo1 largely depend on its pro-fusion forms.
source: This shows that the anti-fusion ubiquitin forms on Fzo1 largely depend on its pro-fusion forms.
evidence: This is supported by data showing that anti-fusion ubiquitylation is reduced in the Fzo1K464R mutant.

claim: Anti-fusion, Ubp2-specific, ubiquitylation on Fzo1 largely depends on Mdm30.
source: Therefore, it is not surprising that anti-fusion, Ubp2-specific, ubiquitylation on Fzo1 also largely depends on Mdm30.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that anti-fusion ubiquitylation depends on pro-fusion ubiquitylation, which is catalyzed by Mdm30.

claim: Mdm30 is not the ligase responsible for the anti-fusion low molecular weight forms on Fzo1.
source: Moreover, it is clear that Mdm30 is not the ligase responsible for the anti-fusion low molecular weight forms on Fzo1 (Anton et al., 2013), which therefore remains to be identified.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Ubp12 and Ubp2 form a regulatory cascade with opposing functions in ubiquitin homeostasis.
source: Our results unravel for the first time a regulatory cascade of two DUBs, Ubp12 and Ubp2, with opposing functions in ubiquitin homeostasis.
evidence: This is the main conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: A 20–40% depletion in ubiquitin levels leads to cellular growth defects under various stress conditions in yeast.
source: A 20–40% depletion in ubiquitin levels leads to cellular growth defects under various stress conditions in yeast, to lethality or infertility in mice, and to neurological diseases like ataxia, gracile axonal dystrophy or Parkinson's disease (Kimura and Tanaka, 2010; Park and Ryu, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: A 20–40% depletion in ubiquitin levels leads to lethality or infertility in mice.
source: A 20–40% depletion in ubiquitin levels leads to cellular growth defects under various stress conditions in yeast, to lethality or infertility in mice, and to neurological diseases like ataxia, gracile axonal dystrophy or Parkinson's disease (Kimura and Tanaka, 2010; Park and Ryu, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: A 20–40% depletion in ubiquitin levels leads to neurological diseases like ataxia, gracile axonal dystrophy or Parkinson's disease.
source: A 20–40% depletion in ubiquitin levels leads to cellular growth defects under various stress conditions in yeast, to lethality or infertility in mice, and to neurological diseases like ataxia, gracile axonal dystrophy or Parkinson's disease (Kimura and Tanaka, 2010; Park and Ryu, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The level of free ubiquitin is adjusted to the cellular needs and is critically regulated by deubiquitylase activity.
source: The level of free ubiquitin is adjusted to the cellular needs, and is critically regulated by deubiquitylase activity (Chernova et al., 2003; Swaminathan et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Δubp12 cells are hyperresistant to cycloheximide (CHX).
source: Δubp12 cells are hyperresistant to cycloheximide (CHX), a chemical inhibitor of protein translation.
evidence: This is directly observed in the spot assay shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Δubp12 cells accumulate conjugated ubiquitin, without affecting the levels of free ubiquitin.
source: Consistently, just like proteasome mutants, also Δubp12 cells accumulate conjugated ubiquitin, without affecting the levels of free ubiquitin.
evidence: This is directly observed in the immunoblot data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Δubp2 cells show a 40% depletion of free ubiquitin and hypersensitivity to CHX.
source: In turn, Δubp2 cells showed a 40% depletion of free ubiquitin and hypersensitivity to CHX, consistent with similar observations in strains presenting decreased free ubiquitin levels (Hanna et al., 2003).
evidence: This is directly observed in the immunoblot and spot assay data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Deletion of UBP2 leads to increased levels of ubiquitin conjugates.
source: Nevertheless, along with reduced free ubiquitin, deletion of UBP2 also clearly led to increased levels of ubiquitin conjugates, as observed upon DmUsp5 depletion in the fruit fly (Kovács et al., 2015).
evidence: This is directly observed in the immunoblot data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Depletion of free ubiquitin is epistatic over the accumulation of ubiquitylated conjugates for cellular growth.
source: Our analysis of Δubp2 cells sheds light on this question, demonstrating that depletion of free ubiquitin is epistatic over the accumulation of ubiquitylated conjugates for cellular growth.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Δubp2 cells are hypersensitive to CHX despite accumulating ubiquitin conjugates.

claim: The removal of ubiquitin from a substrate is generally expected to increase its stability.
source: What could justify the opposite behavior of Ubp2 and Ubp12 in ubiquitin homeostasis and substrate turnover? The removal of ubiquitin from a substrate is generally expected to increase its stability, as observed for Fzo1 in Δubp2 cells.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge.

claim: Ubp2 appears as a general quality control deubiquitylase recognizing both K48- and K63-linked ubiquitin chains that signal for turnover.
source: Consistently, Ubp2 appears as a general quality control deubiquitylase recognizing both K48- and K63-linked ubiquitin chains that signal for turnover, both by the UPS and by the lysosome (Anton et al., 2013; Fang et al., 2016; Ho et al., 2017; Silva et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The turnover of both Fzo1 and Ubp2 is decreased in Δubp12 cells.
source: In contrast, the turnover of both Fzo1 and Ubp2 is decreased in Δubp12 cells.
evidence: This is supported by cycloheximide chase experiments shown in Figures 5B and 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Ubp12 does not stabilize Rad23.
source: Moreover, Ubp12 does not stabilize Rad23 (Gödderz et al., 2017) and Gpa1 (Wang et al., 2005), i.e. its two other known substrates.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Ubp12 does not stabilize Gpa1.
source: Moreover, Ubp12 does not stabilize Rad23 (Gödderz et al., 2017) and Gpa1 (Wang et al., 2005), i.e. its two other known substrates.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Ubp12 exhibits a broad substrate specificity in vitro recognizing both K48- and K63-linked chains.
source: Ubp12 exhibits a broad substrate specificity in vitro recognizing both K48- and K63-linked chains, consistent with previous observations (Schaefer and Morgan, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro deubiquitylation assays shown in Figure 6D and E, and a citation to previous literature.

claim: The ubiquitin signals that accumulate in Fzo1, Ubp2, Rad23 and Gpa1 are all composed of a limited number of discrete bands.
source: Notably, the ubiquitin signals that accumulate in Fzo1, Ubp2, Rad23 and Gpa1 are all composed of a limited number of discrete bands, instead of the high molecular weight smear, typical for polyubiquitylated substrates.
evidence: This is observed in the immunoblot data for Fzo1 and Ubp2, and inferred from previous literature for Rad23 and Gpa1.

claim: For Fzo1, Ubp12 recognizes ubiquitylated forms that only contain two ubiquitin moieties that are linked via K48.
source: For Fzo1, we find that Ubp12 recognizes ubiquitylated forms that only contain two ubiquitin moieties that are linked via K48.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6F.

claim: The protein Met4 is ubiquitylated with a limited number of discrete bands.
source: The protein Met4 was also shown to be ubiquitylated with a a limited number of discrete bands (Flick et al., 2004; Kuras et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: In Met4, intramolecular association with a ubiquitin binding domain shields the ubiquitin chains, thus preventing their elongation and protecting Met4 against proteasomal degradation.
source: In this case, intramolecular association with a ubiquitin binding domain in Met4 shields the ubiquitin chains, thus preventing their elongation and protecting Met4 against proteasomal degradation (Flick et al., 2006; Tyrrell et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Both Ubp2 and Ubp12 are regulated by ubiquitylation.
source: Our findings suggest that this involves ubiquitylation of the DUBs themselves, because both Ubp2 and Ubp12 are regulated by ubiquitylation.
evidence: This is supported by data showing ubiquitylation of both Ubp2 and Ubp12.

claim: Ubiquitylation of DUBs renders them interdependent.
source: This consequently renders DUBs interdependent, as exemplified with Ubp12 being the DUB of Ubp2.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Ubp12 deubiquitylates Ubp2.

claim: Ubp2 ubiquitylation could induce a conformational change favouring catalytic activity.
source: For example, Ubp2 ubiquitylation could induce a conformational change favouring catalytic activity, as observed for the DUB ATXN3 (Todi et al., 2010).
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on analogy to another DUB.

claim: Several residues of Ubp2 were found to be phosphorylated.
source: In addition, several residues of Ubp2 were found to be phosphorylated (Swaney et al., 2013), suggesting that coordinated ubiquitylation/phosphorylation events could increase its activity.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Coordinated ubiquitylation/phosphorylation events could increase Ubp2 activity.
source: In addition, several residues of Ubp2 were found to be phosphorylated (Swaney et al., 2013), suggesting that coordinated ubiquitylation/phosphorylation events could increase its activity.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on the observation that Ubp2 is both ubiquitylated and phosphorylated.

claim: Ubp2 ubiquitylation could favor its interaction with Ubp12 and/or Cdc48.
source: Finally, given that many DUBs often act as part of protein complexes, Ubp2 ubiquitylation could favor its interaction with Ubp12 and/or Cdc48.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on the observation that Ubp2 interacts with both Ubp12 and Cdc48.

claim: Ubp2 ubiquitylation could release autoinhibition by a conformational change, as observed for the DUB Ubp6 upon binding to the proteasome.
source: This could release autoinhibition by a conformational change, as observed for the DUB Ubp6 upon binding to the proteasome, i.e. a AAA+ ATPase like Cdc48 (Hanna et al., 2006).
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on analogy to another DUB.

claim: Cdc48 has been shown to associate with several DUBs.
source: In fact, Cdc48 has been shown to associate with several DUBs (Ossareh-Nazari et al., 2010; Papadopoulos et al., 2017; Rumpf and Jentsch, 2006; Uchiyama et al., 2002) but also recognizes ubiquitylated proteins, consistent with its interaction with both Ubp12 and Ubp2.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: DUB ubiquitylation could allow recruitment of Cdc48 and provide a platform guiding DUBs to their relevant substrates.
source: Therefore, DUB ubiquitylation could allow recruitment of Cdc48 and provide a platform guiding DUBs to their relevant substrates.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on the observation that Cdc48 interacts with ubiquitylated DUBs.

claim: A local regulation of Fzo1 by Cdc48 could allow increased efficiency of the Cdc48-DUB cascade on Fzo1 regulation.
source: In fact, a local regulation of Fzo1 by Cdc48 could allow increased efficiency of the Cdc48-DUB cascade on Fzo1 regulation.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on the observation that Cdc48 directly interacts with Fzo1.

claim: Cdc48 serves as a binding platform allowing cross-talk regulation between DUBs.
source: In conclusion, our results suggest that Cdc48 serves as a binding platform allowing cross-talk regulation between DUBs, bringing new insights into the knowledge of ubiquitin biology.
evidence: This is the conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing that Cdc48 interacts with both Ubp12 and Ubp2.
